definition_used: A journal/publisher/institution states that one or more authors violated one or more of the journal/publisher/institution’s policy(ies). RW will use this reason when no other information about the correction/EOC/retraction is available (i.e., the notice only states that there was a breach of policy), or when the breach of policy (as an additional reason) cannot be addressed by existing reasons.
caution: The definition is intentionally broad and used when no specific policy breach details are available. It signals a policy violation by an author but does not specify which policy, making it a transparency/oversight signal rather than a direct indicator of research content or authorship integrity issues.
semantic_rationale: The definition describes a notice stating an author violated a policy, which is a post-publication transparency signal about a policy breach. It does not inherently indicate problems with research content, authorship, or peer review, but rather a general policy violation. Therefore, it maps to post_publication_transparency_due_process_oversight as a broad oversight category.
